summary: All code is in crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs. (1) `by_rank`: the final sort of `Engine::search` breaks a score tie by date modified, newest first, then by path; the paths are compared as text (`by_path`, review fix). `cut_in_order` puts the list a sort chose back in the same order. (2) `rerank`: +50 (`WHOLE_NAME`, decided by `spells`) when a search's several words spell the whole name apart from separators, with or without the extension. No length gradient, no division. (3) `search_root`: fff-search is asked for 2,000 hits more than are kept (`TIES_AHEAD`), and the hits after the cut that score the same as the last one kept are kept too (`through_ties`), in all three branches (Folder, Any Kind, files); a group that runs on past those 2,000 is cut where it was before. (4) Any Kind no longer calls fff-search's `fuzzy_search_mixed`: the engine makes that search's two searches (`fuzzy_search_directories`, and `fuzzy_search` unless the query ends in a slash) and merges them in order (`best_of_both`), a file and a folder of one score in turn, because the mixed search's unstable sort by score followed by its cut dropped the most recently modified of many equal matches. docs/manual.md: three sentences in Ranking and limits, one clause in the sort paragraph.
changelog: Search results that match equally well are listed newest first, by when they were last modified, and then by path, so a search for `screenshot` or `invoice` starts with the latest files whichever search location they are in. They used to come one search location after another, and in no order inside one when there were many. A search made again now lists the same items in the same order, where a list of many equally good matches could change from one search to the next, and with Any Kind the most recently modified of a few thousand equal matches could be the ones left out; only a search with thousands more equal matches in one search location than it ranks can still vary. A one-letter search of a search location with more than 20,000 files lists folders as well, where it could list files alone. Several words that spell a whole name rank it as an exact match, so `tax return` lists `Tax Return.pdf` ahead of `Tax Return 2024.pdf`.
behaviour_changes: Results with equal scores are listed newest first by date modified, then by path, across search locations. Before, they came one search location after another and inside one in whatever order fff-search returned. Folders and apps, which the index holds no date for, follow the files they tie with and go by path among themselves. Seen in the window (my own pictures, two search locations): `screenshot` listed the first location's nine and then the second's `Screenshot 10.png`, the newest of all, second to last; it is now first of the files. `file` in the stock demo folder lists file-001, 002, 003 ... in order.

The path that settles what the score and the date leave is compared as text (the whole path's bytes), not folder by folder. The two differ only between folders where one's name begins the other's: `a 2/x` now comes before `a/x`, because a space sorts before a slash.

The same search lists the same items in the same order when made again, unless a location has more than 2,000 further hits scoring exactly like the last one kept. In the 77,559-file tree (cargo registry sources, /usr/share, /usr/lib, /usr/include; my 28 searches x Any Kind, files only, Folder, Code = 112, five or six runs each): 84 to 91 of 112 listed other items or another order from run to run on the trunk, 7 to 10 with this commit (the implementer's 28 searches: 93 before, 8 or 9 after). The ones left in my set: `mod` and `test` as Any Kind, files and Code, `src` as Code, `src/` as files, `window` as Any Kind, `index` as Folder.

Lists that came up short or missed better matches because the pool was cut among ties are fuller: `makefile` (Any Kind) 343 hits on the trunk and 499 now; `lib` (Any Kind) lists 319 items scoring 179 or more that the trunk's run did not have, while that run listed items scoring as low as 141.

Several words that spell a whole name rank it as an exact match (+50): `tax return` lists `tax_return.pdf` and `Tax Return.pdf` ahead of `Tax Return 2024.pdf` and `Tax Return - amended draft copy 2.pdf`, whatever their dates (picture). `Return-Tax.pdf` and `taxreturn.pdf` count too, and so does the name with its extension: `tax return pdf`, `cargo toml` (Cargo.toml +50), `lib rs`, `main rs`, `budget csv`. In the demo folder `tax exemption` lists `TaxExemption.object` ahead of `Tax Exemption Certificate.txt`. A single word is unaffected, so the names of a numbered series still tie and their dates decide.

Any Kind with more equal matches in a location than a search ranks: the files ranked are the ones modified last, as Kind and files-only searches always did. Before, the two newest of 4,100 equal files were missing from the list. A file and a folder with the same score are taken in turn there.

A one-letter search (Any Kind) of a location with more than 20,000 items of one score ranks folders and the newest files in turn. It used to rank the newest 20,000 files and no folder: in /usr/share (21,391 files, 2,989 folders) `s` had no folder among its hits on the trunk and has the 1,189 with an s in their names now, among them the folder named `s`, which ranks second. The other side of it: that many fewer of the older files are ranked.

A search ranks up to 2,000 more hits per location when they tie with the last one kept. An older match is no longer dropped for 2,000 newer ones that match no better (an older, shallower `note-old.txt`, or folder `note-old`, now ranks first where it was not listed).

A sort of results looks at up to 20,000 matches per location plus up to 2,000 more that tie with the last (manual updated). The list a sort chooses is returned in the same best-first order as a plain search.
`score` in `fff find` and /v1/find is 50 higher for whole-name multi-word matches. Request and response shapes are unchanged.

One-letter, quoted and sorted Any Kind searches ask fff-search for 22,000 files and 22,000 folders per location instead of 40,000 of each; Kind, files-only and Folder searches ask for 2,000 more hits than before.

Cost. Debug build, the same 112 searches, processor time, the least of 18 alternated runs of each added up, on a machine the other lanes were loading: trunk 5,068 ms, the implementer's commit 5,600 ms (+10.5%), the final code 5,482 ms (+8.2%). The final sort by itself, built alone with `rustc -O` (63,653 paths of the same tree with one date and a handful of scores, which is what a one-letter search ranks there): 2 ms by the score alone, 52 to 74 ms with the paths compared as `Path` compares them (86 ns a comparison, 878,000 of them), 10 ms as text (6 ns).

In the demo folder with a second search location, 120 searches (30 queries x Any Kind, files only, Folder, Code; words, capitals, globs, `src/`, `atlas src/`, `many/ file`, `!file`, quoted phrases, one letter) list exactly the same items on the trunk and on this commit; 36 of them in another order (ties, and the names the bonus moves up), 11 with a whole-name score that is 50 higher.
left_out: CHANGELOG.md: the guide forbids it. The entry is the Changelog (Changed) paragraph of the commit message, repeated in `changelog` here.

Full run-to-run sameness. Where a location has more than 2,000 further hits scoring the same as the last one kept, which of them are ranked is still fff-search's choice: newest first for files, by chance where the dates are equal and for folders. Seeing a whole group costs in proportion to its size; the implementer measured a lookahead of 6,000 making all 112 stable at +29% time against +9.5%, and kept 2,000. It is one constant, `TIES_AHEAD`.
Natural order for the path tie-break (`IMG_2` before `IMG_10` at equal dates): the plan accepts byte order.
Dates for folders and apps: the plan says not to stat directories before the sort, so they follow the files they tie with.

An engine test for the one-letter search's folders: it takes more than 22,000 files in one location, a second fixture the size of the largest there is. `best_of_both`'s unit test pins the turns; the effect was measured (behaviour_changes).
README.md and the Search Syntax dialog: neither states anything about ranking.

Not compiled for macOS or Windows. Nothing cfg-gated was touched; `ends_with(['/', std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR])` is the one platform-dependent expression, mirrored from fff-search. `cargo clippy --features term` was not run: nothing under src/term, and no signature it calls, changed.
No headless UI test in tests/*.rs: the behaviour is the engine's and has engine tests; the window is covered by the pictures.

review_fixes: The tie-break was slow where it matters most. `by_rank` compared the paths with `Path`'s own order, which reads both paths folder by folder: 86 ns a comparison. Where thousands of hits have one score and one date (an unpacked or cloned folder; every folder hit, which has no date) the sort comes to the paths for every two hits it compares. Built alone with `rustc -O`, the sort of the 63,653 hits a one-letter search ranks in the test tree took 2 ms by the score alone and 52 to 74 ms with that tie-break, on every such search; the implementer's debug timings could not show it, since the standard library is optimized in both builds and the engine's own code was the slow part there. Fix: `by_path` compares the paths as text (6 ns; the same sort takes 10 ms), used by `by_rank` and `cut_in_order`. The unit test pins the order with `a 2/` against `a/`.

No engine test made the search the window makes with ties past the cut: `a_match_isnt_left_out_for_others_that_match_no_better` searched files only, so with `through_ties` taken out of the Any Kind branch no engine test failed. The test now makes the search both ways, and fails for the second without it.

The Folder branch had no test either: with `through_ties` taken out of it no engine test failed. New engine test a_folder_isnt_left_out_for_others_that_match_no_better (2,051 folders; fails every time, five runs of five, with the branch's ties not kept).

Commit message: the cost paragraph restated from my own measurements (processor time, which the other lanes' load disturbs less than the clock), the text comparison and its timing, a second set of searches for the run-to-run figures, and what a one-letter search now ranks in a large location, with a sentence for it in the Changelog paragraph.

Rebase onto three new trunk commits (60df179 smart-folder-save-and-leaks, 153eb8f live-search-results, ca4fbee choose-nu-path): one conflict, the `use fff_search::{..}` list in engine.rs, where live-search-results added `WatchEventKind` and this change `Score` and `SearchResult`; resolved to keep all three.
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit d85ca95: 673 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. The implementer's commit was 78672cd on a6b81fc; the trunk moved three times while I reviewed (60df179 smart-folder-save-and-leaks, 153eb8f live-search-results, ca4fbee choose-nu-path), and check.sh was run on top of each rebase (CHECK OK on 153eb8f with 665 and 666 passed, then on ca4fbee with 673). `git push . HEAD:search-ui-polish` fast-forwarded ca4fbee..d85ca95 and `git push origin search-ui-polish` went through; `git ls-remote origin` reads d85ca95.

How it was checked. I read `Engine::search`, `search_root`, `cut_in_order`, `rerank`, `spells`, `by_rank`, `through_ties` and `best_of_both` whole, and fff-search's `fuzzy_search`, `fuzzy_search_directories`, `fuzzy_search_mixed`, `sort_and_paginate` and `sort_and_paginate_dirs`: files come by (score, date modified) with a stable sort, folders by score alone with nothing to order equal scores by, and the mixed search asks for twice the page of each, sorts the two with `sort_unstable_by_key` on the score and cuts. The engine's own merge asks for fetch + 2,000 of each, which holds the best fetch + 2,000 of both, and `best_of_both` stops there, so a list that runs out before that is every match. The tests live beside the code, so instead of reversing the patch I took the change apart: 18 mutations of the final code, each run against the new tests (final sort by score alone; by_rank without the date; without the path; paths compared as `Path` does; TIES_AHEAD = 0; through_ties never falling back; through_ties keeping no ties; no ties kept in the Any Kind branch; none in the Folder branch; `fuzzy_search_mixed` back, with and without the lookahead; best_of_both files first on a tie; a query ending in a slash searching files too; cut_in_order by score alone, and without the date; no whole-name bonus; no extension variant; the wide fetch off). Every one fails a test named for it. Two failed nothing at first, the Any Kind and the Folder branch keeping no ties; with the review's two tests each fails exactly one of the 69 engine tests. The nine new tests and the changed one passed 15 runs in a row at a load average near 8. A scratch example (deleted) ran `Engine::search` over the four roots and wrote each list out; a script checked the 47,447 neighbouring pairs of the 112 lists against (score, date, path as text), none out of order, where the trunk's lists have 2,871. Pictures before and after are my own, on a copy of the demo with a second search location.

The three ways I thought it most likely to hurt someone. (1) Typing gets slower: every keystroke runs this, and the first letter typed is the heaviest search. Found and fixed, see review_fixes; what is left is bounded by 2,000 more hits a location and measured in behaviour_changes. (2) The default search loses results, since Any Kind no longer uses fff-search's own search of both: read against fff-search's source, compared on 120 searches of a small tree (same items every time) and 112 of the large one, where every item the trunk listed and this does not scores no higher than the commit's lowest or belongs to a search that still varies or to a one-letter search (below); and a query ending in a slash still lists folders alone (an existing test fails without it). (3) The ranking gets worse: the whole-name bonus goes only to names that already have every word, so `sort_can_choose`'s premise holds, and it is the single-word exact margin; a one-letter search in a large location now ranks folders at the cost of as many of its older files, which I judge the better half: the trunk could not find a folder at all there.

With the new trunk commits: live-search-results (153eb8f) runs a search again quietly and shows the answer only if it differs from the list on screen in the changed files, or in order after a rescan. Lists now come out the same from run to run except in the cases under Found, not fixed, so fewer are replaced for nothing; nothing there needed changing, and its engine and window tests pass on top of this. smart-folder-save-and-leaks and choose-nu-path don't touch the engine.

For the briefs still to come:
- typo-fallback-near-miss (lane-g, at work): in `Engine::search` the strict check is followed by `rerank` and `raw.sort_by(by_rank)`; put the near-miss check where `strict` is. A location's pool now holds up to 2,000 more hits than `fetch` (those scoring like the last one kept), and for Any Kind it is made of two fff-search results merged by `best_of_both`. Ties in your tests' lists now come newest first and then by path as text. See the second item under Found, not fixed: it is the same cut your change filters after.
- query-history-boost: `search_root` no longer calls `fuzzy_search_mixed`; `qt` goes to `picker.fuzzy_search` in two places (the Any Kind branch and the files branch). fff-search's +1,000 sits in `Score.total`, which `best_of_both` and `through_ties` read, so today the file opened before is first in its list and always inside the cut. If the bonus moves into `Engine::search` and `None` is passed, a file inside a group of ties larger than the cut can be left out before the bonus is added: add its hit if it is missing.
- multi-word-highlights: `rerank` has a new step and a helper `spells(name, words)`; `into_hit` and `highlight` are untouched.
- adhoc-index-feedback, recents-walk-index, search-settings-without-effect, regex-content-search: nothing to do. `by_path` is there if a list of yours needs a cheap last tie-break.
- Anything that changes `fetch` or `TIES_AHEAD`: five fixtures are sized against them (2,051 files, 2,051 folders, 4,050, 4,100 and 21,000 files), and the manual's sort paragraph quotes 2,000.

Found, not fixed:
- A search still varies from run to run where a location has more than 2,000 further hits scoring the same as the last one kept: Kind: Code `mod` in the test tree (about 5,000 `mod.rs` files with one date) shares as few as 62 of 500 items between two runs. See left_out.
- The cut is made by fff-search's score before the strict check. When typo matches score like the strict ones or better, strict matches are cut with them and the list comes out short with no `+`: Kind: Folder `index` in the test tree lists 233 or 234 folders depending on the run, of more that have the letters in order. It was so before; the lookahead only helps where the group at the cut ends within 2,000.
- Of more equal matches than a search ranks, fff-search hands over the newest, while `rerank` would prefer the shallowest: an old, shallow file among many thousands of same-named newer ones is still not a candidate.
- A one-letter search ranks 20,000 items of a location (all of them when it has no more than 22,000), whatever the letter: in a larger location the names with the letter among the rest are not found (now the older files; before this change the older files and every folder).
- Three /tmp/polish-shot-* folders were lying in /tmp when I finished. Every run of shot.sh I made ended well and removed its own; I left these alone.
